name: fuel_element_sphere
title: Spherical fuel element with exponential heat generation
summary: 50-node finite-volume model of a spherical fuel element whose volumetric heat generation decays exponentially from the centre (gen = g```_dot_0*exp(-b*r/r_fuel)), covered by a cladding shell and cooled by convection to a gas at 500 °C; the nodal energy balances are solved together with the analytical solution for a uniform generation (b = 0) for comparison.
language_features: prime/backtick notation in the variable names (not supported by CoolSolve)

origin.notes: Example 1.4-1 of Nellis & Klein, Heat Transfer, Cambridge University Press, 2009, from the EES example set of F-Chart Software; the binary example was saved by EES X11.908. Plain-text mirror published under MIT by EES-Community/ees-examples (commit 5c703d0); the stored solution was extracted from ees-examples-raw/uncategorized/example_1.4-1_fuel_element.eez of the same repository.

verification.summary: Runnable variant vs the EES stored solution (ees-examples-raw .eez): 60 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001); the 203 stored temperature records are stale (value = guess = 1, provably inconsistent with the model's own ConvertTemp/analytics) and were excluded. Profile agrees with the exact continuous solution to 2.0e-4, with the stored N=1000 records to 1.4e-4; energy balance 2.2e-5.
verification.reference: Stored solution of ees-examples-raw/uncategorized/example_1.4-1_fuel_element.eez (EES-Community/ees-examples); analytical solution for b = 0 (in the model) and the exact continuous solution of the exponential-generation sphere
verification.notes: compare_solution.py vs the full stored CSV: 262 common variables, 202 differ (rtol=0.001), only in EES: 2852, only in CoolSolve: 2 — every difference is a stale stored record (value = guess default 1, while T_C[i] = T[i] - 273.15 and C_2 = 1024.4 by the model's own boundary condition; the file also holds leftover records r/T/T_C[51..1000] of an older N=1000 run whose values are physical, e.g. T[1000] = 793.826 K = the CoolSolve surface temperature). On the 60 records that are not provably stale (inputs, grid r[1..50], DELTAr, R_cond_clad, R_conv, N): 60 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001), max rel diff 3.6e-10 on r[12]. C_2 = 1024.397166 K exact against 1024.397165533 (1.2e-13); profile vs the exact continuous solution 2.0e-4 (node 1, 50-node discretisation); vs the stored N=1000 records interpolated at the node radii, 47 nodes, 1.4e-4; energy balance Q_gen = 126.137 W against Q_rej = 126.134 W (2.2e-5).
